source.title: Representation as a Bottleneck for Mechanistic Interpretability: The Manifestation Unit Protocol
source.authors: Hussein Chouman; Wataru Sasaki; T. Matsui; Hirohiko Suwa; K. Yasumoto

page_placements.theme: Mediation concentrates in middle-to-late layers under specified interventions

record.tranche_reason: The study tests aspects of the GPT-2 IOI circuit using a different method: schema-based head retrieval followed by set-overlap and path-patching comparisons. It does not reproduce the original full circuit-discovery or ablation protocol.
record.gate_note: Rows cover GPT-2 IOI-head retrieval and interventions that bear on circuit membership or IOI mediation. The study does not knock out everything outside the 26-head circuit or test each named head class's role individually. Other-behaviour ablation results are recorded as findings outside the listed claim versions; cited circuit findings from prior work are not treated as results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Wang et al. IOI heads as a gold set to score its own retrieval schema. Most GPT-2 rows measure the framework's retrieval or patching performance against that oracle, not whether the circuit holds. The two incidental circuit-level measurements are too coarse to test any version, and the authors present them as framework validation. Per-layer patching is all 12 heads per layer; the 7-head oracle set is patched without the rest of the circuit. These are recorded under fits_no_version. The record's V1/V5 limits_scope labels misattribute retrieval shortfalls to the circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that their typed schema set-recovers known IOI circuit members (5/7 at k=30) and beats random retrieval. They add that per-layer patching reproduces the L7–9 hotspot, but that per-field causal enrichment is null after Bonferroni correction. Their stated contribution on GPT-2 is at the retrieval layer, not strict per-head causal mediation. They attribute the low oracle restoration (0.117) to the IOI circuit being distributed.
record.recipe_differences: This is a schema-based retrieval and validation study, not a reproduction of the original circuit-discovery recipe. It tests overlap with known IOI heads and patches retrieved sets at varying budgets; it does not identify and ablate the full 26-head circuit or test each head class's stated role.
record.method_sensitivity: Path-patching restored fraction varies with retrieval budget k; the study also reports different per-layer mediation and no significant per-field enrichment after Bonferroni correction.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching all 12 heads of a layer at once (BABA corruption, n=80) restores 16.9%, 22.3% and 29.4% of the IOI logit difference at layers 7, 8 and 9. Layers 0–5 contribute marginally; layers 10–11 show small or slightly negative effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-level IOI mediation in GPT-2 small concentrates in layers 7–9.

fits_no_version.finding: A fixed 7-head oracle set described as L7–9 name movers restores only 0.117 of the IOI logit difference under path-patching.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small subsets of the IOI circuit, patched alone, restore only a small fraction of the logit difference.

fits_no_version.finding: Schema-retrieved heads beat matched-budget random heads on induction, IO-routing and bigram mean-ablation shifts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Schema-retrieved GPT-2 heads produce larger intervention effects than matched-budget random heads.

record.problems: The GPT-2 evidence is retrieval and path-patching validation rather than a test of the full 26-head circuit. The canonical 7-head set itself restores only 0.117 of the IOI logit-difference; the 0.409 result uses a 30-head retrieved set, and the authors state that it does not show per-head causal enrichment. Per-field path-patching tests report corrected p-values but not effect sizes. The GPT-2 reference-head recovery results are not separated into IOI-only and non-IOI heads.

untested.parts: No identification or ablation of the 26-head, 7-class circuit. No faithfulness, completeness or minimality tests. No role tests for any head class.
No name-mover ablation and no measure of backup takeover.
Only GPT-2 small. No other models, sizes or checkpoints, and no test of component reuse.
The schema retrieval is not a circuit-finding method compared for recovering the circuit.
No comparison of ablation types, metrics or prompt distributions for the circuit's faithfulness or completeness.
No name-order, template or more-name variants.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' with V1 and V5 limits_scope labels conflates the framework's retrieval shortfalls with properties of the circuit. The study never tests the circuit; it uses the circuit heads as ground truth. The 7-head 'L7–9 name-mover' oracle does not match Wang et al.'s class assignments; the paper's own F.5 list puts name movers at L9/L10 and S-inhibition heads at L7/L8. The R1 value conflict (5/7 versus 0.411) should be resolved in the row.

versions.untested_parts: The exact 26-head, 7-class circuit; completeness and minimality under the original criteria; effects of knocking out everything outside that circuit; and role-specific tests for each head class.
No ablation of main name-movers followed by a test of backup heads taking over.
No comparison across other models, sizes, or checkpoints, and no test that the same components are reused across tasks.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods or ablation types for recovery of essentially the same circuit.
The study varies retrieval budget and reports path-patching results, but does not compare ablation types or prompt distributions for the original circuit.
No systematic comparison across name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

relation.reason: The study uses existing IOI findings to validate its representation framework; the reported results do not test a claim version.

tranche.reason: Known IOI heads serve as reference sets for evaluating schema retrieval and intervention performance. Whole-layer mediation does not establish the circuit's composition, criteria, backup takeover, or equivalence across methods.

source_check.notes: App. F.7 explicitly supplies all five rows' values and their random baseline. The backup-head interpretation is not a takeover experiment; whole-layer effects do not validate the 26-head, seven-class circuit.
